message.content: In the 19th‑century art world, **Auguste Rodin**’s work dominated the conversation about contemporary sculpture.  His monumental bronze “The Gates of Hell” (begun in 1880 and completed in 1917) and the intimate “Kiss” (1889) were both widely exhibited and admired across Europe and America.  These pieces captured the era’s fascination with psychological depth, realism, and expressive form, and they remain among the most frequently cited examples of 19th‑century sculpture today.
